thread:
Maria Chen: quick question — can we add a "quiet window" feature in Console to reduce alert noise for low-severity SLO breaches during late-night hours? we get paged for a lot of per-tenant soft SLOs that could be email-only at 2am.
Kei Sato: +1 on the idea. would prefer it to be rule-scoped (SLO rule -> quiet windows) not global. different services have different tolerances.
Devon Patel: curious how this interacts with routing policies. if a tenant is on a paid SLA we should bypass quiet windows and page regardless.
Sasha Ortiz: agree with both — need per-tenant override + routing policy tie-in. also UX: toggle should show a preview of what notifications would be suppressed.
Maria Chen: exactly — console should show "would notify" vs "would suppress" preview when editing a quiet window.
ops-oncall: ops objection: quiet windows risk missing real incidents. need escalation exceptions: if burst rate > X or error budget burn > Y then ignore quiet window.
Kei Sato: yep add conditional bypasses. propose fields: severity_threshold, bypass_if_burn>%, bypass_if_rate>rps.
Devon Patel: here's a quick config sketch i mocked up:

```yaml
slo_rule:
  id: p99-latency
  threshold_ms: 500
  notify:
    - pager
    - email
  quiet_windows:
    - start: "02:00"
      end: "06:00"
      days: [sat, sun]
      severity_override: email_only
      bypass_conditions:
        error_budget_burn_pct: 5
        sustained_error_rate_rps: 50
  per_tenant_overrides:
    acct-123:
      notify: pager
```

Devon Patel: that covers per-tenant override + bypass conditions.
Sasha Ortiz: UX nit: when someone edits the quiet window, show a small simulation: "in the last 30 days X alerts would have been suppressed" — helps product decide.
Maria Chen: good call. also add an audit log entry in the console and indicate who created the quiet window.
alert-bot: [automated message] example alert that would be affected: "svc-a p99-latency breach for acct-123 (10m)" severity: page
ops-oncall: for SLA customers, we should default to "bypass quiet windows" but allow customer-configurable exceptions. ops wants an allowlist.
Kei Sato: implementation idea: store quiet windows on alerting-config objects, policy routing layer evaluates per request + tenant metadata. runtime checks: tenant_sla -> maybe_bypass, burst detection -> bypass.
Sasha Ortiz: also surface token-level cost/latency impact in the preview? might be noisy but helpful for PMs.
Maria Chen: plan suggestion: 1) add SLO-rule quiet_windows schema + bypass fields; 2) console editor with preview + audit; 3) routing policy flag for tenant allowlist; 4) rollout to internal org via feature flag for 2 weeks, watch missed-page metrics.
Devon Patel: SGTM. i'll draft the PR for schema + evaluator.
Kei Sato: i'll take the console mock and preview sim.
ops-oncall: please include a manual override button on the oncall page to force notify if oncall sees something weird.
Maria Chen: thanks all — i'll file an RFC w/ the config sketch and the rollout plan. tagging @Sasha for UX follow-up. :thumbsup:
